title: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2611.07126v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. While proprietary models can achieve high agreement with human annotators, they remain costly and difficult to deploy in practical settings. Lightweight open-source LLM judges provide an attractive alternative but typically exhibit lower agreement with human ratings. In this paper, we investigate whether soft prompt tuning can align open-source LLM judges more closely with human annotation policy. We train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges across the dimensions of bias, toxicity, and personalization. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over the corresponding untuned baselines. translated_title: 通过软提示调优将大语言模型评审者适配至已观测的人类标注策略
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用作评估聊天机器人回复的自动化评审者。虽然专有模型能够与人类标注者达成高度一致，但其成本高昂且难以在实际场景中部署。轻量级的开源LLM评审者提供了一种有吸引力的替代方案，但通常与人类评分的一致性较低。本文研究了软提示调优能否使开源LLM评审者更贴近人类标注策略。我们在FairBotBench基准上训练软提示，并在偏见、毒性和个性化等维度上对适配后的评审者进行评估。研究结果表明，混合软提示调优——即把文本提示与学习到的连续提示嵌入相结合——相比相应的未调优基线，能够持续提升与人类标注的一致性。对于Qwen 3.5 9B，适配后的评审者超越了托管的参考模型。
tldr: 本文提出混合软提示调优方法，将文本提示与学习到的连续提示嵌入相结合，使开源LLM评审者在偏见、毒性和个性化维度上与人类标注策略的一致性显著提升，甚至超越托管的专有参考模型。
en_tdlr: Hybrid soft prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, aligns open-source LLM judges with human annotation policy, consistently improving agreement with human annotations and surpassing hosted reference models.
